name: Delta Air Lines
blurb: Major U.S. carrier with a large narrow-body and wide-body fleet. Configurations vary by registration and retrofit status.

name: United Airlines
blurb: U.S. network carrier operating domestic and long-haul fleets. Cabin layouts differ across subfleets.

name: American Airlines
blurb: U.S. carrier with extensive A321 and 737 fleets. Seat maps below are schematic reconstructions of typical public layouts.

name: British Airways
blurb: UK flag carrier. Short-haul A320-family and long-haul wide-body configs vary by aircraft and route.

name: easyJet
blurb: European low-cost carrier operating an all-Airbus A320-family fleet with largely single-cabin layouts.

name: Southwest Airlines
blurb: U.S. low-cost carrier with an all-Boeing 737 fleet and primarily single-cabin layouts. Configurations vary by subfleet.

name: JetBlue
blurb: U.S. carrier known for A320-family aircraft and select Mint premium cabins. Layouts differ by route and retrofit.

name: Alaska Airlines
blurb: U.S. carrier operating mainly Boeing 737s. First, Premium, and Main cabin products vary across the fleet.

name: Lufthansa
blurb: German network carrier with short-haul A320-family and long-haul wide-body fleets. Cabin products differ by aircraft.

name: Air France
blurb: French flag carrier operating short-haul narrow-bodies and long-haul wide-bodies. Schematics below are typical public layouts only.

name: Ryanair
blurb: European ultra-low-cost carrier with a high-density Boeing 737 fleet. Single-cabin layouts are typical.

name: Emirates
blurb: Dubai-based long-haul carrier operating large wide-body fleets. Multi-cabin products vary substantially by aircraft and retrofit.

name: Qatar Airways
blurb: Doha-based network carrier with modern wide-body fleets. Business and economy layouts differ by subfleet.

name: Turkish Airlines
blurb: Istanbul-based network carrier with a large narrow-body and wide-body fleet. Cabin products and densities vary by aircraft and route.
